title: A Extraction for the Asset
premise: Tamsin Voss's career is built on talking people out of impossible rooms, but the one failure she carries — a defector named Ilse who vanished mid-flight eight years ago — has been quietly rewritten: every record of the flight now says it never existed. When a new asset, Marek, offers to trade the truth about Ilse for extraction across a shifting border checkpoint, Tamsin realizes the erasure is ongoing and someone inside her own agency is pruning the past. As she runs Marek toward the border, she discovers he is bait, dangled to draw out whoever still protects Ilse's secret — and that Ilse may be alive, running the very operation hunting them. In the climax, Tamsin negotiates not for an exit but for memory itself, forcing the agency to choose between its polished lie and the people it discarded; she chooses loyalty to the living over truth as an abstraction, walking Marek across the border while Ilse disappears again — this time by her own design.
about_author: Odile Halloran is a former crisis-line coordinator who spent a decade listening to people talk their way out of the worst nights of their lives. She writes thrillers about the conversations that decide everything, from a farmhouse in the Ardennes.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A routine hostage negotiation ends in success, but her triumph sours when a junior archivist mentions an anomaly: a flight manifest she remembers personally has been scrubbed. We see her packed go-bag and her polished lie about Ilse. Emotional beat: the past knocking politely before it kicks the door.

chapters.title: Manifest Zero
chapters.summary: Tamsin digs at night, finding that Flight 4412 exists only in her memory and one corrupted backup. Her old handler, Brandt, warns her off with unusual warmth. POV alternates to Marek, a nervous defector in a safehouse, rehearsing a name he shouldn't know: Ilse. Emotional beat: vertigo — the floor of her history is gone.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Marek contacts Tamsin directly: he'll give up the truth of Flight 4412 if she extracts him personally before the border checkpoint rotates shifts in seventy-two hours. Her agency refuses the job; she takes it anyway. Emotional beat: the negotiator becoming the hostage of her own need to know.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Road chapter, Tamsin's POV, with Marek in a borrowed car. They build trust through small trades — her failure story for his forged papers — while a grey sedan shadows them. She notices Marek's tradecraft is too good for a frightened clerk. Emotional beat: found family forming inside a lie neither will name.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Math
chapters.summary: The sedan forces them off-route into a river town; a staged mugging nearly takes Marek's case. Tamsin realizes the attackers wanted the case, not him — inside are Ilse's original debrief tapes. Brandt calls, offering to make everything vanish again if she walks away. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth sharpening into a blade.

chapters.title: The Bait Pattern
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, cold and forensic: the leak, the route, the timing all steer them to one crossing — the same one Ilse's flight was rerouted from eight years ago. Marek confesses he was recruited to lure out whoever kept Ilse's records alive. He believed that person was Tamsin. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as a mirror.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, first appearance: alive, running the agency's erasure unit, the one who scrubbed Flight 4412 — to erase herself from a kill order, not from shame. She has been protecting Tamsin from the file's last page. Emotional beat: the ghost revealed as the most trapped person in the story.

chapters.title: The Room With No Exit
chapters.summary: Ilse's team takes Tamsin and Marek at the border town. In a negotiation room that mirrors her career's defining failure, Tamsin must talk Ilse down from completing the erasure — with Marek's life as the clock. Climax beat: the negotiator finally in the room she's been rehearsing for eight years.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Climax. Tamsin refuses to negotiate for her own record; she negotiates for Marek's crossing and Ilse's freedom from the unit, offering the one currency the agency can't prune: a live witness who won't stop talking. Ilse stands down, burns the kill order, and lets them walk. Emotional beat: truth surrendered as a weapon, kept as a promise.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Marek crosses at the new shift; Tamsin resigns, go-bag finally unpacked. A postcard arrives with no signature — just a flight number that officially never existed. She smiles, keeps the lie polished for the agency, and keeps the truth for her found family. Emotional beat: quiet, chosen memory.
